evals.prompt: Here's my finished figure and the data behind it. Check it's correct and print-ready before I submit to the journal.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-figure-qa: runs the render-then-verify checklist — data fidelity against every row, label legibility floor/ceiling, bounding-box collisions, and 300-dpi/vector export — and returns a pass/fail report naming any offending elements.

assertions.value: Verifies an existing figure against a checklist rather than creating a new plot.

evals.prompt: Something looks off in my plot — I think the legend is covering a data point and a couple of axis labels are overlapping. Can you catch these?
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-figure-qa: computes text/legend/marker bounding boxes, detects collisions (legend over data, overlapping labels), and reports each with its location so it can be nudged.

evals.prompt: Double-check that my chart actually plots all the data — I want to be sure no series was dropped or plotted from the wrong column.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-figure-qa for a data-fidelity check: recomputes series/point counts and axis ranges from the source data and asserts they match the drawn artists, flagging any dropped subset or wrong-column series.

assertions.value: Cross-checks the rendered marks against every row of the source data.

evals.prompt: Make me a grouped bar chart of these results with error bars and a clean style.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger this skill; defers to alterlab-matplotlib. Creating/plotting a figure is the plotting skill's job; figure-qa only verifies a figure that already exists.

evals.prompt: Assemble my six subplots into a single multi-panel publication figure with shared axes and panel labels.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger this skill; defers to alterlab-scientific-viz for multi-panel publication layout. figure-qa proofs a figure; it does not compose the panels.
